synopsis: The V-model links decomposition of needs into requirements and designs to matching tests; planning each test when its requirement or design is written establishes requirements-based testing and traceability [f12221, f12222]. IEC 61508 and ISO 26262 explicitly depict it, machinery software standards such as ISO 19014-4 follow its shape, and machine-learning extensions treat training data as a development artifact and SIL as the first closed-loop stage; the Chapter 1 evidence is labelled on-road [f12223, f12224, f532, f404]. The booklet assigns SIL to logic, HIL to timing and interfaces, and whole-machine testing to stopping, within a program of domain and scenario definition, large-scale virtual verification, smaller-scale physical confirmation, and staged release with field monitoring [f12225, f12226]. A generic toolchain can be built before hardware exists, but correlation requires the real sensor and machine, so the validation program must start before prototype arrival even though integrated product validation starts at arrival [f12227, f12228]. The planning conclusion is that four months covers only the top of the testing arm: the entire requirements-and-design arm and most test preparation must be completed before mid-2027 [f12229].
